      "body": "One part of GDPR is the ability for customers to delete their own data.\r\n\r\nIf this is to become a feature of EDD, I would hope that the actual transaction data wouldn't be deleted completely so reporting isn't goofed up. Perhaps a transaction would simply be attributed to an 'anonymous' customer?"

    {
      "id": 354314553,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-354314553",

      "updated_at": null,

      "body": "I can build this as a plugin, we would need to consider comments, reviews, front end submissions and commissions as well (assuming the “user” is a vendor).\n\nSent from my iPhone\n\n> On 28 Dec 2017, at 16:02, Scott Buscemi <notifications@github.com> wrote:\n> \n> One part of GDPR is the ability for customers to delete their own data.\n> \n> If this is to become a feature of EDD, I would hope that the actual transaction data wouldn't be deleted completely so reporting isn't goofed up.       "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "I was surprised that their post didn’t include any information about any\nchanges they’ll be making to Woocommerce.\n\nOn Thu, Dec 28, 2017 at 9:52 AM John Parris <notifications@github.com>\nwrote:\n\n> WooCommerce has some good info here:\n> https://woocommerce.com/2017/12/gdpr-compliance-woocommerce/\n>\n> —\n> You are receiving this because you commented.\n> Reply to this email directly, view it on GitHub\n> <https://github.com/easydigitaldownloads/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-354327903>,\n> or mute the thread\n> <https://github.com/notifications/unsubscribe-auth/AEIs0DPQ9lGXRMEG3wCzu5LZxeGL0xglks5tE9V1gaJpZM4QviKu>\n> .\n>\n"

    {
      "id": 354330451,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-354330451",
      "created_at": "2017-12-28T18:10:57Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "This should probably be something maintained within EDD itself, I think a plugin would require many people to miss compliance. While it is a requirement for compliance, I'm curious if this would be something that all sites could benefit from.\r\n\r\nWe could include it (which would then easily allow extensions to remove their data via filters, etc), and allow store owners to enable the feature. Thoughts here @pippinsplugins on where it should live?"
    },
    {
      "id": 354353009,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-354353009",
      "created_at": "2017-12-28T20:26:02Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "I am not entirely decided on this but I think I would prefer that this live within an add-on, actually.\r\n\r\nI view GDPR the same way I view VAT, which we do not fully support in core.\r\n\r\nIf we add full support for GDPR then we should likewise add full support for VAT and other country / region specific laws (thinking of Germany here). When do we determine when and when not to support non-global regulations?\r\n\r\nI suppose my main hesitation in adding GDPR specific features is \"when does it stop?\" conundrum?\r\n\r\nAt this time I'd like to propose that compliance features be built through a free add-on that we (EDD) put on an \"officially approved\" recommendation list. This would include creation of FAQs for it on our main documentation portal.\r\n\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 358202577,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-358202577",

      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "I think, with the reasoning above, I agree with @pippinsplugins actually. We would want to be able to work with whoever builds this (if it's not in-house) to be sure it works with all extensions that connect with customer data, so that we do not end up in a non-compliant state due to some extension data not being removed."
    },

    {
      "id": 368351225,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-368351225",
      "created_at": "2018-02-25T22:29:36Z",

    {
      "id": 368937537,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-368937537",
      "created_at": "2018-02-27T16:27:31Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-02-27T16:27:39Z",
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "Right now I'd say we need to see what 'tools' the core team makes available to Plugin developers. There is a lot of talk around a couple solutions:\r\n1) Creating a way to register certain data as private\r\n2) A Request log, for site owners to work through.\r\n\r\nI think one of the important things that EDD will have to monitor is compliance with other eCommerce data laws like VATMOS which requires keeping customer data for a timeframe, however, if that user requests to have their data anonymized/removed, what implications does that have for the store owner to remain compliant from an accounting/tax perspective?\r\n\r\nSounds like the Core team has some ideas moving forward on how to build out some of these 'audit' tools, and if possible I'd prefer that we simply hook into those, instead of building a whole new UI for it.\r\n\r\nI'd for one think that we need to keep transactional data in place. If a user decides to request their data be scrubbed, I feel like we need to keep the payment record mostly in tact however some of the data is important for tax reporting for the business owner (like the billing address) , we could simply scrub the customer data to be anonymous, while still unique.\r\n\r\nhttps://make.wordpress.org/core/2018/02/19/proposed-roadmap-tools-for-gdpr-compliance/"
    },
    {
      "id": 372844610,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-372844610",
      "created_at": "2018-03-13T22:46:40Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 14",
      "body": "> I think one of the important things that EDD will have to monitor is compliance with other eCommerce data laws like VATMOS which requires keeping customer data for a timeframe, however, if that user requests to have their data anonymized/removed, what implications does that have for the store owner to remain compliant from an accounting/tax perspective?\r\n\r\nThe new GDPR law does not trump other EU laws like VATMOS. This means that even though personal data may be scrubbed, the transaction itself including billing address (or at least country?) must indeed remain in the database..."
    },
    {
      "id": 372851801,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-372851801",

    {
      "id": 374921422,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-374921422",
      "created_at": "2018-03-21T12:33:39Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 15",
      "body": "Very interested in how this is progressing, as we use EDD with our BackUpWordPress plugin for Human Made and are working toward GDPR compliance overall. I was trying to pinpoint specific issues or things we would need to track for EDD to be compliant. Has work begun on the addon yet? \r\n\r\nAt this point, specifics already noted above include: \r\n\r\n- ability for customers to delete their own data\r\n- (for the site owner) knowledge of where the information itself is stored and server/database locations\r\n\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 375779110,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-375779110",
      "created_at": "2018-03-23T19:48:04Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 15",
      "body": "Has anyone else put together a full use of all EDD data that is collected for Audit purposes? "
    },
    {
      "id": 375782331,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-375782331",
      "created_at": "2018-03-23T20:01:12Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "@katmoody We're looking into getting a documentation source available for what EDD stores. We're still awaiting some decisions from WP Core to see if they are going to offer us as plugin developers some tools for this, or if we're all going to have to roll this ourselves. I'll put something preliminary together early next week from the EDD side of things."
    },
    {
      "id": 375783241,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-375783241",
      "created_at": "2018-03-23T20:04:57Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-03-25T15:29:49Z",
      "author": "Participant 15",
      "body": "Thank you @cklosowski - We're going through a full review of all our sites and an audit, and I needed to have all the personal data listed for that. As I complete the included EDD info, I will add or link to that list here for you guys, maybe it can be useful for others who are auditing their data as well. \r\n\r\nIt does look like WP Core is considering some hooks/filters that plugin developers can use but I've not gone through the Trac to see what has been done or planned specifically ;-) \r\n\r\nSo far, our audit has revealed the following personal data via EDD, though I'm still looking for anything that will in turn identify a customer or could be combined with other data to identify a customer. I'm not including data used for other plugins though some extension info is included by default (license key and transaction id is mapped to the payment processor for example). \r\n\r\n- Full Name\r\n- User ID\r\n- Customer Email(s)\r\n- Payment ID\r\n- Billing Address\r\n- License Key\r\n- Site Url (license activated)\r\n- IP Address (upon sale)\r\n- Transaction ID (after sale)\r\n- 'Send Product Updates' Update Emails\r\n- Product Receipt (by email automatically, by PDF as requested)\r\n\r\nThe key factor in this audit is to determine what information we actually have, whether we need it and if so, for what legal purpose. As a reminder: \r\n\r\n**Lawful basis for processing**\r\n\r\n1. Consent\r\n2. Necessary to perform contract\r\n3. Necessary to comply with law\r\n4. Necessary to protect vital interests of data subject\r\n5. Necessary in the public interest\r\n6. Necessary for our legitimate interests\r\n\r\nFrom there, we have a spreadsheet to keep all the other information for each data type, like more specific info on why it's needed, who has access, what type of protection it has, etc. \r\n\r\nLet me know if I've forgotten something specific!\r\n\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 376326995,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-376326995",
      "created_at": "2018-03-26T22:04:26Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "@katmoody Some of this data, while unique is not identifiable to a user though. That's the major thing we've got to determine. We cannot, for instance, just remove a transaction ID from a gateway or a billing address (or some subsection of it) due to VATMOS, as that would possibly pull a site owner out of compliance for those taxation laws.\r\n\r\nThis is where it starts getting very conflicted/complex. Some of this data, I believe, has to be in tact (possibly made anonymous?) in order for stores to not break the law as well. Because of some of these things, a customer ID would have to remain (to an anonymous customer) so taxation and what not could be reported correctly if audited by the revenue enforcement.\r\n\r\nI've started our internal doc for our team to review and start auditing. Once we have more we'll get something up publicly so we can move forward."
    },
    {
      "id": 376495341,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-376495341",
      "created_at": "2018-03-27T11:46:12Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 16",
      "body": "I currently got no resource to back any of the following up, but isn't the removal of data based on the 'right to be forgotten'? \r\n\r\nIf thats the case, wouldn't it be only for public data, allowing for orders to remain in tact as private data?"
    },
    {
      "id": 376596572,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-376596572",
      "created_at": "2018-03-27T16:52:19Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "@JeroenSormani From what I can read on the official documentation page (https://gdpr-info.eu/), its' not just about 'public data' but about being able to 'profile' a person based off the data collected. That means while we may have to keep the payment history in tact including transaction IDs, items purchased, some billing address information for taxes, we can likely remove non-necessary data like the name, email address etc and make them anonymous as in while I can build a profile, I cannot tie that profile to a given individual because I now know nothing about who that person is, just that they are a generic 'record' with no means of contact.\r\n\r\nI do have a concern/question that I thought about this morning and that has to do with financial institutions and disputes. For instance, PayPal can allow a dispute up to 180 days after purchase, but a right to request deletion has to be processed within 30 days of request...which means a user could purchase, request deletion and dispute within the valid timeframes.\r\n\r\nThe likely hood of winning a dispute is already low in some cases, but not having any data except the transaction ID could make that difficult. I'm still reading more into this but I'll keep posting my findings/questions once we have more info."
    },
    {
      "id": 376851385,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-376851385",
      "created_at": "2018-03-28T11:18:41Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 15",
      "body": "My reading was that any data that could lead to the discovery of someone's identity. On the Transaction ID and such things, the only reason that they can currently lead to someone's identity is that they are all linked together. Removing the link back to the specific user would likely work, or anonymizing it?\r\n\r\nThe request to be deleted is just that, a request. If the data has to be kept for financial reasons (ie for VAT or tax filings) then my understanding is that the request can be denied for that reason as the other law overrides it. But I'm no lawyer and am just as confused as everyone else on a lot of the info I read. "
    },
    {

      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "This is exactly how I read it...and my perspective on it as well :)\r\n\r\n> The request to be deleted is just that, a request. If the data has to be kept for financial reasons (ie for VAT or tax filings) then my understanding is that the request can be denied for that reason as the other law overrides it. But I'm no lawyer and am just as confused as everyone else on a lot of the info I read.\r\n\r\n@katmoody Thanks for your feedback. I appreciate it greatly.\r\n\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 378448430,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-378448430",
      "created_at": "2018-04-04T01:15:42Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-04-04T01:30:37Z",
      "author": "Participant 11",
      "body": "I'm pretty concerned about this one ourselves, as we also do a lot of business over seas, both in digital downloads and in services and we're letting our lawyer audit our data to conform to GDPR and in general serve our customers better privacy policies, terms of agreements and transparency.\r\n\r\nIf you guys are having trouble distinguishing the international laws and what should be done/not done, especially in regards to \"when does it stop\" and what you should support or not then hiring a lawyer who specializes in these sorts of matters is probably the best idea. I'm certainly not leaving it up to me. Even I have a lot of trouble grasping all the minute details of GDPR, not including VAT or the EU's crazy cookies policy. Thankfully we don't apply to some of those as a U.S based company, and thankfully we have a lawyer that specializes in trademark, privacy and copyright laws.\r\n\r\nThat being said, if you'd like I can maybe advise you on whatever advice she gives me when we've completed our audit which of course is soon since the deadline is looming.\r\n\r\nI know at least my main concern for EDD is either in core or a plugin ability is to give the user some form of opt in to delete their account on the account page, even if some notice displays that certain things like transaction history and such still remains. I imagine some sort of notice either as a shortcode or a popup would display explaining exactly what's kept and not kept in that instance. That's what makes the most sense to me anyway.\r\n\r\nIt's also likely the terms of agreement checkbox will have to be modified in some way as well or there will have to be a second one for privacy purposes. With GDPR you can't have a user agree to a privacy policy agreement if it's included with some other form of contract (i.e terms of agreement), they have to be separated under GDPR compliance.\r\n\r\nForgot that the user needs to be able to download their data generated by EDD as well.\r\n\r\nCore's solutions for GDPR are pretty great, but if your site has the wordpress back-end closed off to users, then that data needs to be able to be accessed say from the EDD account shortcodes page.\r\n\r\nSo if Core adds the things they're wanting (ability to download user data, ability to delete accounts) etc that just needs to be accessed in a way that EDD users can get to it if the admin is closed off."
    },
    {
      "id": 378673089,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-378673089",
      "created_at": "2018-04-04T17:03:31Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-04-04T17:03:37Z",
      "author": "Participant 17",
      "body": "Yep, this is a big concern for us too. From my perspective, EDD has to make sure their software is compliant with EU law when EDD is available for purchase in the EU. Please keep us updated on the plans."
    },
    {

    {
      "id": 378732687,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-378732687",
      "created_at": "2018-04-04T20:22:26Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "We are working on EDD-specific solutions that will compliment WP core's but will also be independent of those.\r\n\r\nWe'll have updates soon. "
    },
    {
      "id": 378780795,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-378780795",
      "created_at": "2018-04-04T23:55:02Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "How about some updates _now_ :)\r\n\r\nI've been spending quite a bit of time looking at the plugins out there that do some of this work (outside of core, but we will support core when things are in a more stable state). Today I finished the first work on an addon for WP GDPR Core\r\nhttps://wordpress.org/plugins/wp-gdpr-core/\r\nhttps://github.com/WP-GDPR/wp-gdpr-core\r\n\r\nThis plugin WP GDPR Core supports a front end shortcode, which allows a person to submit their email address and in turn they get an email with an expiring link to view the data.       "id": 388389443,
      "url": "https://github.com/awesomemotive/easy-digital-downloads/issues/6216#issuecomment-388389443",
      "created_at": "2018-05-11T14:59:05Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-05-11T15:00:26Z",
      "author": "Participant 19",
      "body": "The thing with GPDR is that it requires an easy way for users to delete the data. So just a notice and confirmation like cookie law wont seem to cut it. Or 'you agreed to our terms of service' methodology. \r\n\r\nTo chime in the general discussion before this point and some of the approaches voiced : GDPR shouldnt be treated like VAT - VAT was, and is something that pertains to local tax authorities and their action: For there to be consequences, a local (national) tax authority must think that some site is not paying the taxes due to their government, and then act on it. There first needs to be probable cause for this to happen - just like any citizen in any country being investigated for suspected tax evasion. So the authority must be informed of valid purchases by their own residents, then must conclude that the tax for those valid purchases were not paid that quarter, then initiate the procedure for following up and so on. And the consequences would be according to how that country would handle that VAT avoidance - owed VAT plus a measure of interest and fines applied on top, which would be totally pointless to pursue for small amounts.\r\n\r\nBut GPDR is different - users not being able to delete data is something obvious and it doesnt require reqporting to an authority, or the authority trying to confirm non compliance through long legal procedures and follow up with another series of long legal procedures. An official tasked with investigating such issues can just register and confirm that s/he has no way to delete the data. \r\n\r\nAnd the fine for non compliance is quite serious - nothing like what could potentially result from VAT avoidance.\r\n\r\nFor that, both WP and EDD and any major plugin must have their own way of handling GPDR by default, at least for the default features. Plugins may extend these, but such compliance must not be left to plugins alone. "
    },
